## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design runtime provenance controls that scale across regions and vendors, focusing on drift-resistant policy evolution.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime policy versioning
- SBOM provenance and hardware attestations
- Canary rollouts and multi-tenant isolation
- Drift detection and automated rollback
- OPA/Gatekeeper integration with Cosign/SBOM flows

## Code Example
```rego
package cnf.provenance
default allow = false
allow {
  input.sbom.hardware == "sriov"
  input.attestation.valid
  input.signature.valid
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test policy drift in a live multi-region setup?
- What metrics indicate a failed policy rollout and rollback trade-offs?

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to implement tenant-isolated behavior using sidecar patterns and ConfigMap-driven configuration, ensuring no cross-tenant impact while maintaining per-tenant control over canary deployment parameters.

## Key Concepts

- Namespace-scoped configuration through ConfigMap volume mounting
- Lightweight per-tenant canary routing implementation
- Traffic management via sidecar proxy pattern
- JSON-based configuration parsing and validation
- Percentage-based traffic distribution algorithms

## Code Example

```yaml
# Canary configuration ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: canary-config
  namespace: tenant-1
data:
  canary.json: |
    {"percent":20,"enabled":true}
---
# Sidecar deployment with ConfigMap mount
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: canary-sidecar
  namespace: tenant-1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: canary-sidecar
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: canary-sidecar
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: sidecar
        image: canary-router:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: canary-config
          mountPath: /etc/cnf
      volumes:
      - name: canary-config
        configMap:
          name: canary-config
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical design for per-tenant feature gating in CNF gateways, including secure identity, dynamic policy delivery, and runtime enforcement. It emphasizes end-to-end testability and real-world trade-offs between performance and isolation.

## Key Concepts

- per-tenant policy CRD
- bidirectional gRPC capability negotiation
- in-memory enforcement with cache invalidation
- SPIFFE/SVID-based mutual TLS for control plane–sidecar trust
- canary-friendly rollout and end-to-end validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD blueprint (high level)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: cnffeaturepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                tenantID:
                  type: string
                features:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: cnffeaturepolicies
    singular: cnffeaturepolicy
    kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
    shortNames: [cfp]
```

```yaml
# Sample policy (per-tenant)
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-policy
spec:
  tenantID: tenant-a
  features:
    - QUIC
    - TLS13
    - multiplexing
```

```yaml
# Minimal end-to-end test manifest (one namespace)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: mycnf/gateway:latest
          args: ["--config", "/etc/gateway/config.yaml"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/gateway
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: gateway-config
```

```yaml
apiVersion: "cilium.io/v2"
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-isolation
  namespace: cnf-gws
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      tenantID: "tA"
  ingress:
  - from:
    - sourceSelector:
        matchLabels:

  egress:
  - toEndpoints:
```

```go
func allow(tenant, path string) bool {
  key := tenant + ":" + pathHash(path)
  count, _ := redis.Incr(key).Result()
  if count == 1 { redis.Expire(key, time.Minute) }
  return count <= 100
}
```
